name: Abdullah Amer Al Nahdi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Abdullah Amer Al Nahdi founded and is vice chairman of Nahdi Medical, Saudi Arabia's largest chain of pharmacies.
Nahdi Medical, which had $2.3 billion in 2023 revenue, went public on the Saudi stock exchange in 2022.
Al Nahdi started the company by purchasing two pharmacies in Jeddah in 1986, a year after he graduated from university.
The company has more than 1,100 pharmacies, mostly in Saudi Arabia and some in the UAE.
Nahdi Medical has expanded into offering primary healthcare services through a number of health clinics.
forbes_facts: Saudi Arabia's Bin Mahfouz family purchased half of Nahdi Medical in 2003 through its SEDCO Holding entity; today Saleh Salem Bin Mahfouz chairs Nahdi Medical.

name: Diona Teh Li Shian
forbes_bio: Diona Teh Li Shian is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades.
Her father founded the bank in 1966. Teh died in December 2022 at age 92.
Her father had a substantial minority stake in both Public Bank and insurance firm LPI Capital.

name: Tian Ming
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2012-2026); SEC insider holdings (2024); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2022)
forbes_bio: Tian Ming chairs Hefei Meiya Optoelectronic Technology, a supplier of detection equipment.
Tian made his fortune initially from optical sorters for grains and tea leaves, profiting from China's agricultural boom.
Hefei Meiya went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2014.

name: Phil Shawe
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Phil Shawe is cofounder and co-CEO of translation, language services and AI company TransPerfect.
Shawe owns 99% of the firm, which generated $1.3 billion in 2025 revenue and counts Microsoft and various U.S. governmental entities as customers.
He and his one-time fiancee started the company out of an NYU dorm room in 1992; they initially split the company 50-50.
After a messy court battle, a judge ordered a public auction of the company and in 2018 approved Shawe buying her out for $770 million.
Shawe wants to reform the Delaware Court of Chancery, where the TransPerfect case happened; he's funded campaign ads and written op-eds.

name: S.D. Shibulal
forbes_bio: Infosys cofounder S.D. Shibulal oversees his family office, Innovations Investment Management.
While he stepped down as the company's CEO in 2014, he continues to hold a small stake in the firm.
Shibulal cofounded business incubator Axilor Ventures together with former Infosys colleague Senapathy Gopalakrishnan.
He also chairs The Tamara, a boutique resort chain, which his daughter Shruti founded and runs.
forbes_facts: Along with wife, Kumari, he donates regularly to various causes through two family foundations.
From 1991 to 1996, Shibulal worked with Sun Microsystems in the US.

name: Wong Man Li
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2024)
forbes_bio: Wong Man Li is the chairman and CEO of Man Wah Holdings, one of the world's largest suppliers of recliner sofas best known for its high-end Cheers brand.
It also manufactures and sells mattresses.
In 2005, Man Wah went public in Singapore and became the first Chinese furniture enterprise on the Main Board of the Singapore Stock Exchange.
After delisting in 2009, the company re-listed in Hong Kong the following year.
forbes_facts: He got his start earning $4 a day as a factory worker after arriving in Hong Kong from the mainland's Fujian Province in 1990.
Before a recliner goes into production at Man Wah, it is tested by a machine that pokes it for the equivalent of 72 years of use to see if it stays firm.

name: Zuo Jing
forbes_bio: Zuo Jing is vice chairman of Leader Harmonious Drive Systems, which makes harmonic reducers - the "joints" of robots.
Known also as Leaderdrive, the Suzhou-based company is China's largest manufacturer of harmonic reducers by market cap, with customers such as domestic humanoid company UBTech Robotics.
In February 2026, Leaderdrive agreed to set up a joint venture with Taiwan's auto-parts supplier Minth Group in the U.S. to develop joint modules for humanoids.
Jing joined Leaderdrive in 2014, three years after his younger brother Yuyu, now chairman, founded the company.
Prior to Leaderdrive, Jing worked at several government taxation bureaus.

name: Frederic Luddy
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Fred Luddy, a serial entrepreneur, cofounded enterprise software company ServiceNow in 2004, a few weeks before he turned 50.
At the time, Luddy had just lost a nearly $35 million fortune when his previous employer, Peregrine Systems, filed for bankruptcy.
Advised by Sequoia Capital, Luddy turned down a $2.5 billion acquisition offer for ServiceNow in 2011 and took it public the next year.
Luddy stepped down as CEO in 2011 to serve as chief product officer, a role he held until 2017. He became chairman of the board in 2018.
ServiceNow generated $9 billion in revenue in 2023.

name: Vladimir Ivanov
forbes_bio: Vladimir Ivanov is one of the earliest employees at Yandex, a tech company best known for its search engine.
Yandex divested its Russia-based business and delisted its shares from the Moscow stock exchange in 2024.
Yandex was renamed Nebius Group; it now trades on the Nasdaq and builds and operates AI data centers.
Ivanov is one of the largest individual shareholders of Nebius; its shares more than quadrupled in its first year of trading.
Nebius has been able to finance its AI data center business model with $2.8 billion in cash from the Yandex split.

name: Nancy Lerner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Nancy Lerner owes her riches to her billionaire dad, Al Lerner (d. 2002), and to his banking fortune.
Al started his career as a furniture salesman, invested in Cleveland-area real estate and bought control of Equitable Bancorp in 1981.
Equitable Bancorp and Maryland National formed the credit card giant MBNA, whose 2005 merger with Bank of America created a $35 billion enterprise.
The Lerners bought the Cleveland Browns in 1999 and sold the team to Jimmy Haslam for about $1 billion in 2012.

name: Qin Qingping
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2018-2022); Hurun China (2017-2022)
forbes_bio: Qin Qingping chairs Jinneng Science & Technology, a supplier of chemical and coal chemical products.
Jinneng listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2017.
Qin worked for a city government in Shandong Province before he started his own business in 1998.
Jinneng means "golden energy" in Chinese.
